Okay, so I need to figure out which main course was on the dinner menu at Virtue restaurant & bar in Chicago on March 22, 2021, but wasn't there anymore on April 21, 2021. The user mentioned that they went there on their birthday in March and had a delicious main course, but when they returned a month later, that same main course wasn't on the menu anymore. They want to use the Wayback Machine to find out which course it was.

First, I should probably go to the Wayback Machine and look up the menus for those specific dates. I'll start with March 22, 2021. I'll search for Virtue restaurant & bar and find the snapshot from that date. Once I have that, I'll check what the main courses were listed as.

Next, I'll do the same for April 21, 2021. I'll search for the same restaurant and find the snapshot from that date. I'll compare the two menus side by side to see which main course is present in March but missing in April.

I should list out the main courses from both dates. If I see a course that's on the March menu but not on the April menu, that's the one the user is looking for. I'll make sure to note the exact name as it appears on the menu to avoid any confusion.

I might run into issues if the Wayback Machine doesn't have snapshots for those exact dates, but I'll try to find the closest available dates around March 22 and April 21 to ensure I have the most accurate information possible.

Once I have both menus, I'll go through each item one by one. If I find a main course that's only on the March menu, that's the answer. I'll double-check to make sure I didn't miss any items or make any transcription errors.

If I'm unsure about any of the menu items, I might look for images or descriptions that could help confirm the names. Sometimes, the Wayback Machine includes more than just text, so I can cross-reference the text with any images or additional information available.

After identifying the missing main course, I'll present the name clearly, as the user requested without articles like "the" or "a." I'll make sure it's in the correct grammatical form, using the singular since it's a specific dish.

I should also consider if there were any errors in the process, like if the Wayback Machine was slow or unresponsive, which might have caused delays in retrieving the information. If I encountered any technical issues, I'll note that as a potential mistake, but since I was able to manually verify the menus, I think the main issue was just ensuring accuracy in transcription.

In the end, I'll confidently state the main course that was present in March but not in April, knowing that I've cross-verified the information from reliable sources.
